_doc: Share-lost rate of a good while it travels or waits, as a continuous decay rate per year (the share lost over t years is 1 - exp(-rate * t)). Goods not listed do not spoil. Rates are labelled estimates, confidence C or D; a storage and handling model per good would derive them.

wheat_kg.source: Granary loss to pests, rot and rodents, 5-15 per cent a year (the same figure as GRAIN_SPOILAGE_RATE_PER_YEAR in sim/world/agriculture.py).

milk_kg.source: US Dairy (usdairy.com), 'How long can milk sit out' (https://www.usdairy.com/news-articles/how-long-can-milk-sit-out, opened): 'perishable foods like milk should not sit out of the refrigerator or cooler for longer than two hours', and 'if the temperature is above 90F (32C), it should be discarded after one hour'. That is a safety limit for pasteurised milk, hours not days; a rate of 300 a year loses 56 percent in a day, the milder souring reading for raw milk in a cool dairy, so it is a ballpark, not an upper bound.

meat_kg.source: FAO, Methods of meat preservation without refrigeration (https://www.fao.org/4/T0562E/T0562E04.htm, opened): meat from unchilled carcasses 'ripens rapidly' at high temperature; the page gives no days. A rate of 100 a year is e-folding every 3.7 days, an order-of-magnitude ballpark for warm weather (labelled estimate).

hide_kg.source: CSIRO Meat Technology Update 98-3 'Short-term Preservation of Hides and Skins' (https://meatupdate.csiro.au/data/MEAT_TECHNOLOGY_UPDATE_98-3.pdf, opened): Table 1 maximum storage period of chilled hides 1 day at 20C, 2 days at 15C, 5 days at 10C; 'there will be deterioration within one day if hides are left at body temperature for several hours'; 'In sunny or hot weather the risk is very high'. Unsalted, unchilled hides in a warm climate are taken at 1.5 days (mean of 1 day at 20C and 2 days at 15C), so the rate is 365 / 1.5 = 243 a year (was 3, no source). Salted hides keep many months; this row is the green hide.

olive_oil_kg.source: Bertolli, Olive oil shelf life (https://oliveoil.bertolli.com/olive-oil-shelf-life/, opened): unopened extra virgin 'an approximate 16-month shelf life', other companies claim up to 24 months. 1 / 1.33 years = 0.75 and 1 / 2 = 0.5; midpoint 0.625 a year (was 0.15, no source). Modern bottled oil, an analogue for sealed amphorae.

wine_common_kg.source: Craftabrew, How long does homemade wine last (https://craftabrew.com/blogs/the-tap/how-long-does-homemade-wine-last, opened): fruit wines 'best enjoyed within six months to one year', grape wines 'can last one to two years or longer with proper storage', with opened wine 'one to three days' unrefrigerated. Grape wine midpoint 1.5 years, so the rate is 1 / 1.5 = 0.67 a year (was 0.2, no source). Strong resinated wine keeps longer; this row is common wine.

cheese_kg.source: Wikipedia, Cheese (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheese, opened): 'Hard cheeses, such as Cheddar and Parmesan, last longer than soft cheeses', a protective rind gives 'long storage life', and ageing 'lasts from a few days to several years'. A rate of 0.3 a year is e-folding in 3.3 years, a ballpark inside 'several years' (no weight-loss rate found in any opened page).

bread_kg.source: Clemson Cooperative Extension, Food Storage: Pantry, HGIC 3525 (opened): bread 'Use within 3-7 days'. Midpoint 5 days, so the rate is 365 / 5 = 73 a year (e-folding in 5 days; was 50).

salted_meat_kg.source: FAO, Methods of meat preservation without refrigeration (https://www.fao.org/4/T0562E/T0562E04.htm, opened): jerked beef (charque, dried and salted) 'keeps for months at ambient temperatures and is resistant to insect infestation and mould growth'; biltong 'will keep for a year if stored in airtight packaging'. A rate of 0.5 a year loses 39 percent in a year, a ballpark for open storage.

fish_kg.source: FAO Fisheries Technical Paper (https://www.fao.org/4/v7180e/V7180E0c.htm, opened): for tropical fish 'the average relative rate of spoilage ... stored at 20-30C was approximately 25 times higher than at 0C'. No days at ambient are given on the page; a rate of 200 a year is e-folding in 1.8 days, a ballpark for warm weather (labelled estimate).

salted_fish_kg.source: No salted-fish page gave a duration (Wikipedia Salted fish, opened, gives none). Taken by analogy with dried, salted meat: FAO, Methods of meat preservation without refrigeration (https://www.fao.org/4/T0562E/T0562E04.htm, opened), charque 'keeps for months at ambient temperatures'; a rate of 0.6 a year loses 45 percent in a year, a ballpark.

garum_kg.source: Cooking Chew, 'Does fish sauce go bad' (https://cookingchew.com/does-fish-sauce-go-bad.html, opened): unopened fish sauce lasts 'two to three years' (a modern bottled product). Midpoint 2.5 years, so the rate is 1 / 2.5 = 0.4 a year (was 0.1, no source). A modern analogue for sealed amphorae.

silk_cocoon_kg.source: FAO, Silk reeling (http://www.fao.org/4/x2099e/x2099e04.htm, opened): 'the fresh cocoons should arrive at the stifling unit within two to three days after harvest'; pierced cocoons are unfit for reeling. Midpoint 2.5 days, so the rate is 365 / 2.5 = 146 a year (was 20, no source).

silkworm_eggs_kg.source: Bivoltine diapause eggs hatch after about four months of cold storage at 5C (SciELO Brazilian Archives of Biology and Technology, https://scielo.br/j/babt/a/hcJtbZ3nMvMPRLfcm3FZd3Q/, opened). Four months is a third of a year, so the rate is 3 a year (was 2, no source).
